title: Periplus project settings
description: periplus.settings.yml, at the root of the repository being mapped. Committed and reviewed like source. It is the only place a person edits anything the map depends on, and it holds what no pack can know. A general settings file holds what is true for a machine or a user; this one wins where they disagree.

packs.description: Named, not implied by what happens to be on disk. A pack shipped inside a downloaded module loads because this list names it, not because it is present — which is also the whole of the trust story for third-party packs. Not required: a project nobody has configured has no `packs` key at all, which is the file `periplus init` writes and the state `periplus status` exits 0 on. `minItems` is what keeps the other case refused — a key present and empty is a claim that no pack applies, which is a different statement and one no run should accept quietly.

pack_paths.description: Extra directories to resolve packs from, beside the ones the tool ships. A pack a person writes for their own repository is found the same way a bundled one is, or third-party packs are second-class by construction.

folders.description: Overrides the pack's defaults for this repository. Exported configuration is the case that proves it: three real Drupal sites keep it in three different places, one of them computed in PHP at runtime.

first_party.description: Path-based, needing no pack, so a dependency published tomorrow still stops at the boundary. This is also where a dependency is deliberately promoted to first-party, which is the boundary mechanism under test: one line, no engine change.

extensions.description: The last word over any pack. An extension can have no correct global meaning — .inc is PHP here and Pascal somewhere else — so the only place that settles is the project.

values.description: Named text values that no pack can know, such as the module path a project's packages sit under. Every template of every pack may name one as {name}, as it names a path value: a rule's id template, and the template of a file type's path value, so a path value can read {module}/{dir}. A name a loaded pack also gives as a path value, or that a rule captures, is refused when the map is made, and so is a path value template that names a value neither its pattern nor these values give.

re_include.description: Takes back a pack's exclusion without forking the pack. It has to exist for the same reason the extension override does: a pack states a convention, and one repository is always the exception.

rule.description: pack.rule_name, matching the `rule:` key of the rule that failed.

accepted_unknowns.description: Gaps accepted as permanent. Dynamic dispatch, a computed string, an id assembled at runtime. This cannot live in the map, which is generated and must never be hand-edited. Same shape as a lint suppression, and it is what lets an unresolved count reach zero and mean something.
